common_name: Crimson Butterflies Gaura (Compact Red-Stemmed Pink-Flowered Gaura)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or fall; in zone 9 plant February-April or September-November. Crimson Butterflies is a compact gaura cultivar with distinctive dark red stems and foliage.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil — gaura demands excellent drainage and thrives in dry, sunny conditions but declines in consistently moist or heavy soil. Crimson Butterflies is a notably compact gaura cultivar with dark burgundy-red stems and foliage that contrast strikingly against its cloud of small, dancing, rose-pink flowers, a more colorful and diminutive alternative to the taller, green-stemmed species and larger cultivars like Siskiyou Pink. Its smaller stature suits the front of a sunny border or a container where a full-sized gaura would sprawl too much. Cut back by about one-third in midsummer if the plant becomes too open, which stimulates fresh, compact growth, and expect essentially continuous bloom from spring through frost once established.

common_name: Filigran Russian Sage (Finely Cut Lacy Silver-Foliage Russian Sage)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline to neutral, dry to moderately moist soil in full sun; Filigran is an older German-bred cultivar valued for its especially finely cut, lacy silver foliage.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Russian sage will not survive in heavy clay or wet soil and is particularly susceptible to crown rot in humid summer climates if planted in poorly drained sites. Filigran bears unusually finely dissected, lacy, silver-gray foliage even more delicate in texture than standard Russian sage, giving the whole plant an especially airy, feathery look before its hazy lavender-blue flower spikes open from midsummer through fall. Strongly deer-resistant and exceptionally drought-tolerant once established, it attracts bees and butterflies and provides a fine-textured silvery accent among coarser-leaved sun perennials. In well-drained, raised-bed conditions or gravelly soils it is reliably perennial in the Gulf South; cut the woody framework back hard in late winter each year to keep growth vigorous and compact.

common_name: Little Trudy Russian Sage (Compact Rose-Pink Russian Sage)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline to neutral, dry to moderately moist soil in full sun; Little Trudy is an unusual pink-flowered, compact Russian sage cultivar rather than the typical blue-purple.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Russian sage will not survive in heavy clay or wet soil and is particularly susceptible to crown rot in humid summer climates if planted in poorly drained sites. Little Trudy is a compact, mounding Russian sage cultivar bearing soft rose-pink flower spikes rather than the lavender-blue typical of the species, a distinctive color break bred to expand the color range of a plant usually associated only with blue and silver tones. Its silver-gray, aromatic, finely cut foliage still provides the same misty texture as other Russian sage cultivars, and its compact size fits smaller borders better than full-sized species plants. Strongly deer-resistant and exceptionally drought-tolerant once established, it attracts bees and butterflies through a long midsummer-to-fall bloom season.
